crm_notes:
Context: AurumLedger is a regulated payments platform evaluating Redwood Dedicated for transaction-class chat, risk-scoring reranking, and embeddings for fraud detection. Primary ask: firm throughput guarantees and predictable billing for reserved capacity. Finance wants caps and clear overage rules. Security requires KMS + VPC peering + SOC2/ISO alignment.

Throughput negotiations (current):
- Aurum asks for a minimum sustained tokens/sec guarantee to size reserved GPUs. Initial request: 2,500 tokens/sec sustained for chat workload (avg input 220 tokens, output 180 tokens).
- Redwood proposal: baseline 2,200 tokens/sec sustained per cluster with 30% headroom; burst allowance up to 5x baseline for 90s windows, subject to concurrency caps.
- Concurrency caps discussed: target 120 concurrent user sessions (chat), with queueing/backpressure beyond cap. Customer wants soft-fail/queue vs hard 429s.
- Reserved GPU planning: Aurum prefers guaranteed nodes. POC ran on 4 x A100 nodes -> observed 2,800 tokens/sec for conversational pipeline (LLama2-chat-13B-quant). Extrapolation -> ~8 x A100 for 5k sustained with buffer. Agreement leaning to start with 8 reserved GPUs, scale to 12 for peak.
- Latency SLOs: Aurum requests p95 < 150ms non-streaming (512 tok), p99 < 300ms. Redwood prefers p95 < 120ms, p99 < 250ms on pinned capacity; negotiation around streaming vs non-streaming semantics.
- SLA and credits: Aurum pushing for 99.95% uptime + token-delivery SLO credits for throughput degradation. Redwood legal pushed back on strict monetary credits tied to tokens/sec shortfalls; proposing service credits tiered to outage windows.
- Bursts/overage pricing: Need clear step-down model: overflow routed to lower-cost model (smaller quantized family) or queue. Customer requires deterministic cost calculation for overflow periods.
- Failover / degrade strategies: Redwood proposed automatic fallback to a smaller model variant + optional model-compression profile to preserve latency within SLOs during capacity events. Aurum requests explicit routing policy for high-risk transactions (never fallback for high-value fraud checks).

POC artifacts/metrics:
- 2026-02-14 live load test (drive:/AurumLedger/poc/Throughput-Test-Results-2026-02.xlsx): 90-minute test, synthetic mix: 60% chat, 30% embeddings, 10% reranking. Observed sustained tokens/sec: 2.8k on 4xA100 for chat-heavy mix; embedding throughput limited by CPU pre/post-processing; reranking latency tight at 110ms median.
- Fireflies 2026-02-15 meeting (ff_20260215_aurum-poc) contains ask list and decision matrix.

Sales notes / negotiation points to push internally:
- Offer a two-window SLA: baseline sustained guarantee for committed capacity + short high-burst allowance (5x for up to 90s) with metering that excludes known maintenance windows.
- Define explicit concurrency semantics: soft queue (30s max) before 429s for chat; priority queue for flagged transactions (fraud/risk) with guaranteed slice.
- Pricing model: commit to X GPUs + a capped burst buffer (hourly billing for bursts beyond cap at pre-agreed rate). Finance needs example month calc.
- Technical ask: provide workload-specific perf profile (tokens/sec per GPU by model family + sequence length distribution) for contract appendix.

Customer quotes / paraphrases: "We need predictable token throughput so treasury ops don't get hit with surprise charges during peak settlement windows."  /  "If you can guarantee the 2.5k sustained with a clear burst policy, we can move to a 12-month reserved commit."

Next immediate action: prep appendix with measured tokens/sec per GPU (by model family) and two SLA draft options (strict credits vs tiered credits) for 2026-03-16 legal review. Follow-up call scheduled 2026-03-18 to present revised SOW.

short_summary: Enterprise payments platform evaluating Redwood Dedicated. Primary negotiation: guaranteed tokens/sec baseline, concurrency caps, bounded burst policy, reserved GPU sizing and SLA credits. POC shows promising throughput; need final SOW and legal signoff.
internal_recommendation: Offer 8 GPU reserved starting point + optional burst buffer for first 90 days; provide model-by-model tokens/sec appendix. Accept soft queue semantics and explicit priority routing for high-risk transactions. Legal to review tiered credit model.
